subject: Urgent: elevated streaming latency — guidance & next steps (NovusAI)
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novusai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.in>
Cc: support@novusai.com
Date: 2028-08-03T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Chat responses slowing down across streaming sessions

Hi Soojin —

We started seeing streaming responses for our customer-facing chat widgets slow down yesterday (~16:00 UTC). Tokens are arriving in delayed bursts (200-400ms gaps) and in some sessions the stream stalls for multiple seconds before resuming. This affects latency-sensitive features where we show progressive responses.

We attached a small sample of request/response IDs and timestamps (novusai_request_logs_0803.txt) — hope it helps. We tried switching to non-streaming completions as a fallback and that restored throughput but increased end-to-end latency. Can Redwood share any immediate mitigations we can flip on while you triage? Also interested if this is limited to a region or model family.

We have a mid-day demo on Monday and would like a short mitigation path before then.

Thanks,
Tom
Product Ops | NovusAI
--
Tom Hayes
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.in>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>
Date: 2028-08-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Chat responses slowing down across streaming sessions

Tom — thanks for the clear report and the logs. We see the same token pacing on our internal traces for the US-west streaming shard serving model rwd-3b-quant. Initial notes and immediate mitigation options below: 

Quick mitigations (apply immediately):
- Use non-streaming (polling) completions for critical paths (you already tried this; it’s safest short-term).
- Reduce max_tokens and lower concurrency per connection from 8 -> 4 to reduce KV-cache pressure.
- Add our request header X-Redwood-Prefix-Cache: enable to surface prefix cache hits (may reduce first-token latency for repeated prompts).
- Temporarily pin to rwd-3b (non-quant) which has lower per-token tail latency for short sessions (we can route you to a warmed pool).

We are actively triaging root cause. I’m copying Marissa and Ben to coordinate capacity and a warmed fallback. Can you send a few more request IDs from affected sessions and confirm region (us-west/us-east)? Also please include any client-side retry logic you have in place.

We’ll follow up with a short incident page and next steps within 60 minutes.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.in>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.in>
Date: 2028-08-03T17:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Chat responses slowing down — NovusAI (triage)

Team — forwarding Tom’s note and sample logs. Tagged INF-9812 in the tracker. TL;DR: token pacing and intermittent stalls observed across US-west serving pool for rwd-3b-quant; appears correlated with a kernel scheduler change rolled 03:30 UTC earlier today.

Immediate action plan (I applied the first two items):
1) Route NovusAI traffic to warmed rwd-3b pool (done at 17:02 UTC) — monitor for reduced tail.
2) Increase per-connection timeout and reduce concurrency quota for the tenant to 4 connections to lower KV cache churn (done).
3) Engineers to rollback kernel scheduler tweak on affected shard if metrics don’t improve in 20m (Ben / Jonas).
4) Enable request-level prefix cache header for NovusAI to reduce cold-starts (Marissa).
5) Customer comms: Soojin to send a crisp mitigation note and offer credits if SLA impacted.

I attached the triage_runbook.pdf with step-by-step commands and the request id list we received. Please update INF-9812 with any changes.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.in>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.in>
Date: 2028-08-04T02:10:00Z
Subject: Post-incident update: reduced latency & next steps (NovusAI)

Tom — quick update and apologies for the disruption. Summary of what happened and what we did: 

What we observed
- Intermittent token pacing and multi-second stream stalls impacting progressive token delivery for NovusAI sessions routed to the US-west rwd-3b-quant shard.
- Issue onset ~2028-08-02 16:00 UTC with higher incidence during the afternoon traffic spike.

Root cause (short summary)- A kernel-level scheduler change (rolled out during a performance tweak window at 03:30 UTC) changed thread preemption behavior on a subset of GPU hosts, increasing tail latency for attention-kernel calls under certain concurrency patterns. This increased KV-cache pressure and produced the token-delivery pattern you saw. Full technical postmortem is linked below.

What we did
- Immediately routed your traffic to a warmed rwd-3b pool with stable latency (17:02 UTC).
- Reverted the scheduler tweak on affected hosts and rebalanced traffic (17:40 UTC).
- Applied conservative per-connection concurrency limits and enabled prefix caching for your tenant.

Current status
- We observed a 90% reduction in multi-second stalls for your test sessions after the remediation. We continue to monitor for regression and have applied a safety rollback window.

Compensation and next steps
- We will apply a partial SLA credit for the affected hour(s) under your Dedicated contract; details will follow from billing.
- I filed INF-9812 and drafted the technical postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9812 and published a customer-friendly postmortem: https://status.redwood.in/incidents/INC-20280803. The full internal postmortem (postmortem_INC-20280803.md) is attached.

Immediate mitigations for NovusAI (recommended)- If you need low-latency progressive rendering for the demo:
  * Use warmed non-quant rwd-3b model (we can keep a warm pool for you through Monday).
  * Keep streaming timeouts above 10s and cap per-connection concurrency at 4 while we complete the follow-up testing.
  * If progressive UI is critical, use short completion windows with the prefix cache header enabled.

Apologies again for the disruption — I know this interrupted your demo prep. We’ll continue to keep you posted and I’ll reach out tomorrow with the finalized credit details and a slightly longer-term mitigation plan (kernel rollout guardrails + expanded warmed pools).

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
